<h2>Validate Available Core Count</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Verifies that the number of cores (distinct pollen sites) in the
current spatial window meets the minimum required for analysis.
The check is intended as an early guard in the pipeline, applied
directly to 'data_coords' (output of 'extract_dataset_coordinates()') before any
expensive community-data processing begins.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>validate_available_core_count(data_coords = NULL, minimum_core_count = 2)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="data_coords">data_coords</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame of site coordinates, one row per core, as returned by
'extract_dataset_coordinates()'. Gridpoints are already excluded by that function, so
every row represents a real pollen core.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="minimum_core_count">minimum_core_count</code></td>
<td>
<p>A single positive numeric value specifying the minimum number of
distinct cores required. Typically sourced from
the configured minimum core-count threshold.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Raises a 'cli::cli_abort()' error naming the actual core count and
the required threshold when 'nrow(data_coords) &lt; minimum_core_count'. This
causes the targets pipeline target to fail immediately, preventing
all downstream community-data targets from running for spatial windows
that contain too few sites.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>'TRUE' invisibly when the check passes.
</p>


<h3>See Also</h3>

<p>[extract_dataset_coordinates()], [filter_community_by_minimum_core_count()]
</p>

</main>
